rationale: C25 is a close substantive and drafting analogue: both are brief cablegrams to a foreign leader conveying the President's and American people's condolences upon the death of that country's president. They share the same compact sequence—formal addressee, first-person expression of regret or sympathy, condolences to both the leader and the national people, identification of the deceased president, and signature. C15 and C12 are weaker condolence templates because one concerns an ambassador's death and the other a natural disaster.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I wish to express to the people of Austria and to you personally my profound sympathy and that of the people of the United States at the death of President Koerner.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: On behalf of the American people and myself I send sincere condolences to both you and the people of Finland in the loss of President Paasikivi
shared_material.explanation: Distinctively parallel condolence formula addressed simultaneously to the recipient and the recipient's people, conveying sentiments on behalf of both Eisenhower personally and the American people after the death of a national president.

shared_material.child_excerpt: His Excellency Julius Raab Chancellor of Austria
shared_material.parent_excerpt: His Excellency Urho K. Kekkonen President of Finland
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same terse diplomatic cablegram format, beginning with the foreign leader's formal title and proceeding directly to a single condolence paragraph.
